name: Yasuaki Shimizu
discourse_profile: Sound as texture moving through space. Shimizu's central preoccupation is the physical behavior of sound in an environment — "What captivates me is the texture of sound, how it moves within a space, and my relationship with time as the sound floats through it." A childhood experience hearing thousands of insects creating "a wave of electronic sound" near Mt. Fuji seeded this orientation. His studio method is intuitive and non-premeditated: he gathers whatever instruments come to mind and produces sounds according to mood, interested in "the actual sounds that arose out of silence," visualizing the mixing console as a "miniature garden" where harmonics dance. His Bach cello suites project made the philosophy explicit — recording solo saxophone in quarries, mines, and palazzos to "play the space" as a resonating instrument. Jazz training (Ornette Coleman, Rahsaan Roland Kirk) gave him improvisational reflexes — "how to turn on a dime" — but he treats all his influences (jazz, electronic, world music, classical) as "a single organic material" rather than separate traditions to navigate between. His basic approach, established during Utakata no Hibi and Kakashi in the early '80s, has remained fundamentally unaltered: take a simple theme and challenge it through improvisation.
